questions.caseText: A 62-year-old male smoker with a 40 pack-year history presented with a two-month history of progressive difficulty swallowing, initially for solids and later for soft foods, with a sensation of food sticking behind the mid-sternum, accompanied by 9 kg of unintentional weight loss, a chronic dry cough, and recent streaks of blood in his sputum. On examination, there is dullness to percussion with reduced breath sounds over the right anterior chest. Upper GI endoscopy showed extrinsic compression of the mid-esophagus with intact mucosa, and a chest X-ray revealed an opacity in the right lung, right hilar enlargement, and a widened carina. A contrast CT of the chest demonstrated a 5cm mass in the middle lobe. Bronchoscopic biopsy sampling of the subcarinal node confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the right middle lobe with mediastinal and supraclavicular nodal spread.
questions.explanation: Printed answer: Compression of the esophagus due to the tumor resulting in difficulty of swallowing

questions.question: An electron micrograph of a terminal bronchiole shows non-ciliated cells with dome-shaped apical surfaces containing secretory granules. Which of the following is a key function of these cells?
options: Acting as progenitor cells for bronchiolar epithelial regeneration
Producing mucus to trap inhaled particles
Transporting mucus toward the upper respiratory tract
Releasing neuropeptides to regulate airway activity
Phagocytosing inhaled microorganisms and cellular debris

options: FEV1 decreased; FVC increased; FEV1/FVC decreased
FEV1 decreased; FVC decreased; FEV1/FVC increased
FEV1 decreased; FVC increased; FEV1/FVC decreased
FEV1 increased; FVC increased; FEV1/FVC increased

questions.question: What changes in the following will occur after the transition to artificial ventilation of this person?
questions.printedAnswer:
• Total Ventilation: Stays the same because the frequency increased and the tidal volume
decreased proportionally
• Alveolar Ventilation: Decreases as alveolar volume decreased from 500-150 to 250-150.
• Dead Space Ventilation: Increases as dead space is always 150ml so it is not affected by
the tidal volume decrease, and frequency increased
questions.caseText: During normal spontaneous breathing the respiratory parameters of a healthy 25 year old male are measured as: Tidal volume= 500 ml, Respiratory frequency= 16 breaths/min. Following a thorax injury, breathing becomes very painful for this individual. To reduce the magnitude of the chest movement and reduce the pain, the doctor decides to ventilate him artificially using a ventilator with a smaller tidal volume and higher frequency than the spontaneous breathing. His tidal volume is set to 250 ml and respiratory frequency to 32 breaths/min. What change in total ventilation, alveolar ventilation and dead space ventilation of this person will occur after transition to the artificial ventilator?
questions.explanation:
Printed answer: • Total Ventilation: Stays the same because the frequency increased and the tidal volume
decreased proportionally
• Alveolar Ventilation: Decreases as alveolar volume decreased from 500-150 to 250-150.
• Dead Space Ventilation: Increases as dead space is always 150ml so it is not affected by
the tidal volume decrease, and frequency increased

questions.question: What changes on Alveolar PO2 will occur after transition to artificial ventilation?
questions.printedAnswer: It will decrease due to decreased alveolar ventilation
